title: MyLinden Help: Automatic Debit and the Patient Payment Plans Setup Fee
content:
**How does automatic debit affect the setup fee on a Patient Payment Plans plan?**

The autopay share of the setup fee is 0.80 when the plan's automatic debit method is ACH and the patient's Patient Financial Account shows no late fee posted less than 12 whole months before the signing date; it is 0.90 when the method is card or HSA/FSA card and the account shows no such late fee; and it is 1 in every other case.

The autopay share multiplies the tier's setup fee within the scheduled setup fee. It acts on the tier's setup fee itself, and the scheduled setup fee is carried unrounded until the fee is entered.

**What records decide the share?**

- The plan's automatic debit method (ACH, card, HSA/FSA card, or none).
- The late fees on the patient's Patient Financial Account ledger, by posting date, in the period of less than 12 whole months before the signing date.

**The share for each combination**

| Automatic debit method on the plan | Late fee on the Patient Financial Account posted less than 12 whole months before signing | Autopay share |
|---|---|---|
| ACH | None | 0.80 |
| ACH | One or more | 1 |
| Card or HSA/FSA card | None | 0.90 |
| Card or HSA/FSA card | One or more | 1 |
| None | None | 1 |
| None | One or more | 1 |

**Examples (hypothetical dates and fee).**

- A plan signed on 20 September, paying by ACH, on an account whose latest late fee was posted 11 whole months before that date: the late fee falls inside the period, and the share is 1.
- The same plan on an account whose latest late fee was posted 13 whole months before signing: no late fee falls inside the period, and the share is 0.80. On a hypothetical tier setup fee of 40.00, this share alone makes the scheduled setup fee 32.00.
- A plan paying by HSA/FSA card on an account with no late fee at all: the share is 0.90.
